title: To Adapt or Not to Adapt, That is the Ski Question

statements.text: If 𝛼 ≥ 1, i.e., the cost of querying the reverse map is greater than a database lookup, the optimal deterministic strategy is to adapt immediately after the false positive repeats ⌊𝛼⌋ times and is 2-competitive.
For 𝛼 < 1, the optimal offline strategy is to not adapt if 𝑘 =1, and adapt immediately if 𝑘 > 1.
For 𝛼 < 1, adapting immediately achieves a competitive ratio of (1+𝛼).
For 𝛼 < 1, adapting on the second false positive achieves a competitive ratio of (2+𝛼)/(1+𝛼).
For 𝛼 < 1, the optimal strategy is to adapt immediately when 𝛼 < 0.618 and adapt on the second occurrence otherwise.
A strongly √︁ adaptive filter augmented with the ski rental algorithm never returns more than (1+ ⌈𝛼⌉) (𝑛𝜖 +𝑂 ( 𝑛𝜖log𝑛+log𝑛)) false positives with high probability. √︁

For this case, the optimal offline cost is 𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 , i.e., adapt on the first occurrence and avoid the ⌊𝛼⌋𝐶𝐷𝐵 cost from repeated false positives. In this case, the algorithm is 2-competitive as the competitive ratio is: ⌊𝛼⌋𝐶𝐷𝐵 + (𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 ) 𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 ⌊𝛼⌋𝐶𝐷𝐵 = +1 𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 𝛼𝐶𝐷𝐵 +1 ≤ 𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 𝐶𝑅𝑀 +1 ≤ 𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 ≤2 as 𝛼 =𝐶𝑅𝑀 /𝐶𝐷𝐵 □

We first analyze the offline optimal cost. For 𝑘 = 1, the offline optimal cost is 𝐶𝐷𝐵 as it avoids the reverse map lookup. For 𝑘 ≥ 2, the optimal strategy is to adapt on the first occurrence for a cost of (𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 ). Any algorithm that adapts later incurs at least two false positives and would have a cost ≥ 2𝐶𝐷𝐵 . Since 𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 = (1 +𝛼)𝐶𝐷𝐵 < 2𝐶𝐷𝐵 , the optimal strategy is to adapt immediately for a cost of 𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 . □

For 𝑘 =1, the offline optimal cost is 𝐶𝐷𝐵 from Lemma 2. Since adapting immediately costs 𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 , the competitive ratio for 𝑘 = 1 is (𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 )/𝐶𝐷𝐵 = (1 +𝛼). For 𝑘 > 1, this algorithm is optimal (1-competitive) as it immediately adapts. Thus, adapting immediately has a worst-case competitive ratio of (1+𝛼). □

For 𝑘 =1, the offline optimal cost is 𝐶𝐷𝐵 from Lemma 2. Since this algorithm does not adapt, it is optimal and 1-competitive for 𝑘 =1. For 𝑘 > 1, this algorithm incurs a cost of 𝐶𝐷𝐵 + (𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 ) = 2𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 as it adapts on the second occurrence. The offline optimal cost from Lemma 2 is𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀. 2+𝛼 𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 The competitive ratio for this case is therefore 2𝐶 𝐶𝐷𝐵 +𝐶𝑅𝑀 = 1+𝛼 . Since (2+𝛼)/(1+𝛼) > 1, adapting on the second false positive has a worst-case competitive ratio of (2+𝛼)/(1+𝛼). □

By equating (1 + 𝛼) = 2+𝛼 1+𝛼 , the worst-case competitive ratios for adapting immediately(Lemma 3) and on the second occurrence repsectively(Lemma 4), we get a threshold value of 𝛼 =0.618 that indicates which strategy to use: adapt immediately if 𝛼 < 0.618 and on the second occurrence otherwise. To complete the proof, we must also eliminate strategies that allow for more than 2 false positives and adapt on the third false positive. Adapting on the third occurrence or later has a worst-case competitive ratio ≥ (3+𝛼)/(1+𝛼). This ratio is always greater than (2+𝛼)/(1+𝛼), the worst-case Proc. ACM Manag. From [3], a strongly adaptive filter never returns more than (𝑛𝜖 +𝑂 ( 𝑛𝜖log𝑛 + log𝑛)) false positives with high probability. From Theorem 1 and Theorem 5, using a ski rental algorithm for adapting never repeats a false positive more than (1 + ⌈𝛼⌉) times: for 𝛼 ≥ 1 and 𝛼 < 0.618, the ski rental algorithm allows 1+ ⌊𝛼⌋ ≤ 1+ ⌈𝛼⌉ occurrences, and for 0.618 ≤ 𝛼 ≤ 1, it allows 2 =1+ ⌈𝛼⌉ occurrences. Therefore, √︁ a strongly adaptive filter with a ski rental algorithm will never return more than (1+ ⌈𝛼⌉) (𝑛𝜖 +𝑂 ( 𝑛𝜖log𝑛+log𝑛)) false positives with high probability. □
